title: Predict a position and a range
target: Predict a future position and explain the limits of the prediction.
criteria: Use matching units and include the starting position.
Report a central prediction and its bounds.
Distinguish a measurement range from model limitations.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A rover starts at −5 m and moves at +4 m/s for 3 s. What is predicted final position?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A probe starts at 2 km and moves at 500 m/s for 4 s. What is final position in km?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Initial position is exactly 3 m. Velocity is 2.0 ± 0.2 m/s and time is exactly 5 s. What are central final position and bounds?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Independent bounds are x₀ = 4 ± 1 m and v = 3 ± 0.5 m/s, with t = 2 s exact. What is the final-position interval?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A calculated interval comes from bounded measurements and a constant-velocity assumption. What does it omit unless explicitly modeled?
options: All measurement variation already included in the bounds.
Changes in velocity caused by forces.
cpa.guide: Input uncertainty does not automatically cover errors in the motion model.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A prediction gives a bounded position interval. Does that alone establish a 95% probability of being inside it?
options: No; ranges never contain any useful information.
No; a probability needs an additional statistical model.
Yes; every endpoint is equally probable automatically.
cpa.guide: Bounds constrain values under assumptions but do not specify probabilities.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
